sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Read each noun with its article as one word. Do not pause between der, die or das and the noun.
items: der Tisch, die Tür, das Fenster
der Stuhl, das Bett, die Möbel
sections.lede: The article is part of the word, not an extra word in front of it.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: By the end of this lesson you will be able to recognise noun gender and form the plural.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Every German noun has a grammatical gender, and the article shows it: der, die or das.

blocks.text: Gender in German is a property of the word, not of the thing. A table is masculine (der Tisch), a door is feminine (die Tür), and a window is neuter (das Fenster). There is no single rule that predicts every noun, but there are strong patterns, and those patterns cover a large part of the vocabulary you meet at A1.
Das ist ein Tisch, und das ist eine Tür.
blocks.en: That is a table, and that is a door.

items: The three genders are masculine (der), feminine (die) and neuter (das).
The plural article is always die, for all three genders: die Tische, die Türen, die Fenster.
Grammatical gender does not always match natural gender: das Mädchen (the girl) is neuter.
Learn each noun as a trio: article + noun + plural. Der Tisch, die Tische.

blocks.title: Why this matters
blocks.text: The article changes with case, and adjectives take their endings from it. If you know the gender, you can build correct accusative and dative forms later. If you do not, every later case becomes a guess.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: Use the endings as clues, then check the dictionary when a noun is new.

rows: die Zeitung, die Freiheit, die Freundschaft
die Schule, die Frage, die Blume
der Montag, der Januar, der Sommer
der Mann, der Vater, der Sohn
der Lehrer, der Fahrer, der Verkäufer

items: The plural article never changes: der, die and das all become die.
Umlaut is common in plurals but not automatic: das Haus → die Häuser, der Apfel → die Äpfel.
Nouns ending in -er often keep the same form in the plural: der Lehrer → die Lehrer, das Fenster → die Fenster.
In a compound noun, the last part decides the gender: das Haus + die Tür = die Haustür.

blocks.title: Exceptions are normal
blocks.text: Most nouns in -e are feminine, but der Junge, der Name and das Ende are masculine or neuter. Treat the ending as a clue, not a guarantee, and confirm new nouns in a dictionary.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Six nouns from one room, with all three genders and two plural patterns.

items.exampleEn: The table is made of wood.
The chair stands by the table.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Say each sentence with its article. The article tells you the gender.

items.note: der Tisch → ein Tisch in the nominative.

items.en: The table is made of wood.

items.note: die Tür is feminine, so the article is die.
das Fenster is neuter and keeps the same form in the plural.
Plural nouns take die and the verb sind.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: The umlauts in Tür, Stühle and Möbel are the sounds to watch.

items.hint: Round your lips for ü, then say ee: tüür. Keep the r soft.
Tish. The final sch is a clean “sh”, and the i is short.
FENS-ter. The first e is open and the -er is soft.
SHTY-luh. Start with “sht”, then the rounded ü, then a weak final e.
MUR-bel. Round your lips as if to say “oh”, then try to say “e”; do not say “moh-bel”.

blocks.text: In a German dictionary a noun is listed with its article and plural: Tisch, der, -e. That is not extra information; it is the word. Learners who memorise Haus, Tür, Fenster without articles often speak fluently but choose the wrong article under pressure.

Grammatical gender can look odd from outside. Das Mädchen is neuter because the ending -chen makes every noun neuter, and das Fräulein works the same way. German also uses er, sie and es for objects, so a chair can be er and a door can be sie. This is grammar, not a comment on the object.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: A prospective tenant looks at a flat. Listen for der, die and das.

lines.speaker: Kundin
lines.de: Der Raum ist groß. Und das Fenster?
lines.en: The room is big. And the window?

lines.speaker: Maklerin
lines.de: Die Küche ist dort. Sie ist klein, aber hell.
lines.en: The kitchen is over there. It is small but bright.

lines.speaker: Maklerin
lines.en: The furniture stays in the room.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: der, die, das — and the plural die
sections.lede: The definite article changes with gender, but the plural has only one form.

items: The article agrees with the noun, not with the English word: die Tür, even though English “door” has no gender.
In the plural, the article is always die and the verb is sind: Die Stühle sind neu.
The indefinite article has only two forms in the nominative: ein for masculine and neuter, eine for feminine.
A compound noun takes the gender of its final part: die Haustür, because die Tür is feminine.

sections.tip: Write new nouns on cards with a coloured article: der blue, die red, das green. The colour does the remembering for you.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the article or plural that belongs to the noun.

exercises.explanation: die Tür = the door. Tür is feminine.
das Fenster = the window. Fenster is neuter.
Nouns ending in -ung are feminine: die Zeitung.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of das Haus?
exercises.explanation: das Haus takes -er and an umlaut: die Häuser.

exercises.prompt: What is the plural of die Tür?

options: because natural gender always decides the article
because the ending -chen makes a noun neuter
because all short words are neuter
exercises.explanation: The ending -chen always makes a noun neuter, regardless of natural gender.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type der, die or das — or the correct plural form.

exercises.explanation: der Tisch is masculine, and it starts the sentence, so Der takes a capital.
The plural article is always die, for every gender.

exercises.prompt: Die ___ sind neu. (plural of der Stuhl)
exercises.explanation: der Stuhl → die Stühle, with an umlaut and -e.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Keep the article directly in front of its noun.

exercises.explanation: Subject first, then the verb ist, then the adjective neu.
die Tür is feminine, so the indefinite article is eine.
Plural nouns take die and the verb sind.
die Möbel is plural, so the verb is sind.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen to the room description twice, then answer.
sections.speaker: Two neighbours talking about a living room

script.speaker: Herr Ali
script.de: Der Tisch ist schön. Ist er neu?
script.en: The table is nice. Is it new?

script.speaker: Frau Berg
script.de: Ja, der Tisch ist neu. Die Stühle sind alt.
script.en: Yes, the table is new. The chairs are old.

script.speaker: Frau Berg
script.de: Das Bild ist von meiner Tochter.
script.en: The picture is by my daughter.

questions.explanation: Frau Berg says: Ja, der Tisch ist neu.

questions.prompt: What does Frau Berg say about the chairs?
questions.explanation: She says: Die Stühle sind alt — the chairs are old.
Das Bild ist von meiner Tochter — the picture is by my daughter.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Describe the room you are in, using all three genders and one plural.
sections.prompt: Say four sentences about your room. Name at least one masculine, one feminine and one neuter noun, plus one plural.

model.de: Das ist mein Zimmer. Der Tisch ist klein. Die Tür ist weiß. Das Fenster ist groß, und die Stühle sind alt.
model.en: This is my room. The table is small. The door is white. The window is big, and the chairs are old.

tips: Say the article and the noun as one unit, without a pause: derTisch, dieTür, dasFenster.
Check the plural article: it is always die, whatever the singular was.
Record yourself and listen for the umlauts in Tür, Stühle and Möbel.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: Most article errors come from guessing instead of learning the noun with its article.

items.why: Tür is feminine, so it takes die in the nominative.
Haus is neuter: das Haus. The plural is die Häuser.
A plural subject takes the plural verb sind, not ist.
Fenster is neuter. Its plural is also die Fenster, with no ending change.

sections.title: Lesson assessment
sections.lede: Ten questions. Score 70% or more to unlock the next lesson.

questions.explanation: der Stuhl = the chair. Stuhl is masculine.
das Fenster is neuter. Tür and Möbel are feminine, Tisch is masculine.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of das Kind?
What is the plural of das Auto?
questions.explanation: Many nouns of foreign origin take -s: das Auto → die Autos.

questions.prompt: Which noun is feminine because of its ending?
questions.explanation: The ending -schaft makes a noun feminine: die Freundschaft.
die Tür is feminine, and the sentence starts with the article.
der Stuhl is masculine, so the indefinite article is ein.

questions.prompt: Die ___ sind neu. (plural of das Fenster)
questions.explanation: das Fenster keeps the same form in the plural: die Fenster.
Subject first, then the verb ist, then the adjective.
The plural article is die, and the plural verb is sind.
